11.4c — MC Practice 3 + Written-Response Drill

The last practice before exam eve: a mixed set under compressed time, then a timed written-response block with your PPR — the same 60-minute pairing the real exam gives you, in miniature. Today you rehearse STAMINA, not just facts.

Practice Set 3 ~25 min

15 mixed questions, 13 minutes — tighter than real (100s avg → 50s target trains pass 1 speed). All six CED families, three-pass method REQUIRED (bubbling discipline now, so it is reflex on May 14).

Score → error table v3, cumulative across sets 1–3. Your REAL study plan for the weekend comes from this table, not from your feelings about the exam.

WR Block ~25 min

Timed, PPR in hand, phone in bag: 4 prompts in 25 minutes (exam gives 60 for 4 with more writing — we compress to build the muscle):

  1. WR1-style: foreign code excerpt — describe input, behavior, output (11.3 drill two, timed now)
  2. WR2a-style: your algorithm, from your PPR
  3. WR2b-style: your difficulty + specific fix
  4. WR2c-style: your list's role in the program

Trade and grade with the claim-evidence-because rubric (11.3): does every answer name its evidence? Does anyone's WR2b name all three (bug, cause, fix)? Score each other like the College Board would — generous grading in practice is mean in May.

Bug Hunt: Final week traps

  1. Your error table says "algorithms" across all three sets. What does a READING error look like vs a KNOWLEDGE error (tracing? pseudocode syntax? off-by-one?) — and which do you fix by drilling vs. re-reading?
  2. You wrote your WR answers faster than 6 minutes each. What did the rubric lose (evidence quotes) — and why does speed kill WR scores but help MC?
  3. Tomorrow is 11.5 — exam eve, logistics only. What belongs on your weekend study plan: everything, or the two families in your table? (You know.)

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Run pass-1 speed under 60 seconds per question
  • Complete 4 WR prompts inside 25 minutes with evidence
  • Show error tables v1–v3 and name your two weak families
  • Write your weekend plan from the table, not the vibes
